content:
Laredo police will draw blood from DWI suspects who refuse breath tests during Halloween weekend under a three-day "no-refusal" enforcement operation, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The operation launches Friday ahead of Halloween and runs through Sunday, November 1.

Under the program, drivers suspected of driving while intoxicated who refuse a breath specimen may have officers seek a search warrant for a blood draw, with the blood sample used as investigative evidence in prosecution, the Times reported. District Attorney Isidro "Chilo" Alaniz framed the approach as applying where a driver refuses to cooperate and there are indicators of intoxication.

The operation is a partnership involving the Webb and Zapata County District Attorney's Office, Doctors Hospital of Laredo, which handles the blood draws and analysis, and local courts, which handle the warrant paperwork, according to the Times.

Assistant Chief Ricardo Gonzalez said police would no longer simply ask for a voluntary breath specimen and urged parents to watch their children while trick-or-treating, the Times reported. Alaniz called DWI pervasive and noted Halloween's added risk because children and families are out; he said the long-term goal is year-round no-refusal operations, though the program currently focuses on dates such as Halloween.

Police Chief Miguel Rodriguez said 34 additional officers would patrol Saturday in a full-detail operation emphasizing DWI enforcement, supported through a partnership with the Texas Department of Transportation, and said keeping children safe during Halloween festivities was the top priority, according to the Times.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times, "LPD to draw blood from DWI suspects who refuse breath tests on Halloween," October 29, 2026

title: LPD to draw blood from DWI suspects who refuse tests in Halloween no-refusal operation
